scenes.headline: How one GPU serves a 753B-parameter model
scenes.sub: FreeToken measures two bandwidths and lets them split the work.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Piston! FreeToken serves a seven hundred and fifty-three billion parameter model from one workstation GPU. Here's how.

scenes.text: Don't pick an offloading strategy. Measure two bandwidths on the machine, and let them split every decode step's cache misses between PCIe and the CPU.
scenes.say: The idea: don't pick an offloading strategy. Measure two bandwidths, and let them split each step's cache misses between the bus and the CPU.

scenes.title: One decode step, one MoE layer

steps.say: At each layer, the router picks experts. Hits in the GPU cache run at once; the cache follows the router, least recently used out.
The m misses can be fetched over the bus, or computed on the CPU, where their weights already live.

steps.note: both branches at once; no approximation
steps.say: FreeToken does both at once, then merges the partial sums exactly.

scenes.title: The one equation
scenes.say: Balance the two branches so they finish together.

parts.note: host-side expert bandwidth, from the same memory
expert size cancels: a property of the machine

scenes.label: the right share of misses to fetch, across ordinary consumer hardware
scenes.note: two RTX 5090s with different hosts want opposite designs
scenes.say: On ordinary consumer machines, the right share to fetch swings from twenty-five to ninety-one percent.

items.say: Prefill loads the next whole layer while the GPU computes this one, before routing is even known.
Recurrent state is checkpointed at special tokens, where agent harnesses edit, so only the new suffix is recomputed.
And the GPU cache can resize mid-session, because the CPU pool is the source of truth.

scenes.text: Replace decisions with measurements: the bandwidths on this machine, not a spec sheet, decide the split.
